newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Lukewarm response to Caltex Sri Lanka unit debut.
newsitem.headline: Lukewarm response to Caltex Sri Lanka unit debut.

text.p: Shares in Lanka Lubricants Ltd, the Sri Lankan subsidiary of oil company Caltex, began trading on Monday but no deals were reported in the frist 1-3/4 hours due to a mismatch between buyers and sellers, brokers said.
Buyers sought the shares at 40 rupees while sellers cited 55 rupees at the mid-morning break. In July, the company made an initial public offer of 11.7 million shares at 50 rupees each.
"Sellers are only willing to give the share at 55 rupees. Buyers will have to come closer if they want to trade," said Mano Tittawella of brokerage Lanka Securities.
Brokers said many investors had expected employees, who got free shares, to sell at below the issue price. In July, employees issued a statement saying that they would not sell at a discount.

The government sold a 51 percent stake in Lanka Lubricants to Caltex in 1992. Ten percent of the company's issued capital was given to employees in November 1995 under the country's privatisation formula.
The public offer was the portion that was in state hands.
Caltex is a joint venture of Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
